subject: AccraHealth DPA: LLM usage boundaries, no-training ask, and proof of controls
messages:
From: Aisha Mensah <aisha.m@accrahealth.org>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Kwame Boateng <kwame.boateng@accrahealth.org>, Procurement <procurement@accrahealth.org>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA questions — LLM training / output ownership

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the DPA redline. A couple of items came up in our legal and product review we'd like to clarify before we proceed to signature:

- No-training / model improvement: our clinicians must be assured that patient interactions processed by Redwood will not be used to train or improve models. Can you confirm a contractual "no-training" commitment and describe operational controls you will provide as evidence?

- Prompt & response ownership: we need explicit language that the prompts and the model responses generated for our tenant are considered customer data and that AccraHealth retains rights to those outputs for our internal use.

- Cross-border flows: some telemetry and backups may touch third countries for support. We require the dataflow diagram and the list of subprocessors who might handle PII or model outputs.

Attached is a short dataflow diagram and our standard DPA checklist. Can you point us to an evidence pack (SOC2 report, subprocessor attestations, KMS residency details) we can share with Procurement?

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Mensah
Head of Legal, AccraHealth

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mensah <aisha.m@accrahealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — LLM training / output ownership

Hi Aisha,

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to a contractable no-training commitment for AccraHealth interactions; yes to customer ownership of prompts/responses as output IP; and yes we will provide a subprocessor list and a focused evidence pack.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll circulate a tight DPA addendum clause that: (a) commits Redwood to not use AccraHealth tenant data to train models or improve underlying models (no adaptive training) and (b) confirms AccraHealth retains output ownership for prompts and generated responses.
2) Marissa (cc'd) will describe the operational controls to onboard this as an "opt-out" profile (how it is implemented in Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments).
3) David will attach the SOC2 / KMS residency notes and a short subprocessor table for your procurement team.

Can we aim to have the addendum and evidence stub back to you by EOD Wednesday? If that timeline doesn't work, tell me your preferred cutover.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mensah <aisha.m@accrahealth.org>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 10:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — LLM training / output ownership

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the diagram — helpful. A quick operational note from the product side on implementing the no-training / output custody commitments:

- Implementation model: For AccraHealth we recommend Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) or a Dedicated pool pinned to your tenant. In both modes we can ensure request-level routing that sets a "no-learn" flag on requests from your tenant.
- What the flag does: prevents telemetry used for model improvement (gradients, model checkpoints, upstream fine-tuning datasets) from including these inputs; also disables long-term prompt logs from the training pipeline. Short-term ephemeral KV caches still operate for latency but are purged after 24 hours and not retained in model update stores.
- Evidence we can provide: an ops playbook excerpt (audit logs showing no-learn flag), a runbook for subprocessor gating, and an excerpt from our kernel scheduler proving isolation for pinned pools. We attached a checklist named no-train-evidence-checklist.xlsx with items we commit to deliver.

Notes on ownership language: the DPA addendum will state that generated outputs are customer data and Redwood assigns a non-exclusive license back to the customer for internal use. If you need broader IP assignment language, flag it now and Rishi will route to Legal.

For the subprocessor list: operationally the only subprocessors who may touch raw prompts or outputs are the Dedicated host provider (if Dedicated) and our managed backups vendor. If you go Private on-prem, subprocessor exposure is minimal and we can enumerate to your procurement.

Happy to hop on a short call with your security lead to walk the playbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Product — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Kwame Boateng <kwame.boateng@accrahealth.org>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Mensah <aisha.m@accrahealth.org>, Procurement <procurement@accrahealth.org>
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2028 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA questions — LLM training / output ownership

Thanks — helpful detail. A couple quick follow ups from Procurement / Security:

- Evidence pack: can you provide the most recent SOC2 Type II (redacted if needed) and a short attestation that the "no-learn" flag is enforced end-to-end (including any subprocessors)? We also require a KMS residency note confirming keys for AccraHealth tenant data will remain in-region or in an agreed jurisdiction.
- Language ask: procurement prefers "Redwood will not use, train, finetune or otherwise incorporate AccraHealth data into model training or model improvement activities, including through automated telemetry or human review processes." Can you accept that as-is or suggest edits?
- Timeline: Procurement needs these docs to run the vendor security assessment by Friday 07/06. Is that feasible?

If you can send a short package (SOC2 stub, KMS residency note, subprocessor table, and the DPA addendum text) by COB Wednesday 07/03 we can start parallel review.

Regards,
Kwame Boateng
Head of Procurement, AccraHealth

On Wed, Jul 3, 2028 at 16:22, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Kwame — see attached SOC2 summary (redacted) and the subprocessor table. Regarding the proposed contract language, we can accept the procurement phrasing with a small carveout: we will ensure no AccraHealth tenant data is used for model training or human-in-the-loop review, but we need a mutually agreed exception for aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry used for platform reliability improvements (strictly no PII / no customer prompts). We can add a short clause and a logging/audit capability to provide transparency.
>
> KMS residency: for Dedicated we can pin keys to your cloud region and provide KMS attestation. For Private deployments keys remain under customer control.
>
> I'm attaching the SOC2 excerpt and the updated subprocessor list. Rishi will circulate the DPA addendum text in the next hour.
>
> Cheers,
> David
> Head of Trust & Security
> Redwood Inference
